final.executive_summary: Hold the Underweight and execute one modest trim at the next session open, rebalancing AAPL from the current 2.51% weight to a target_weight_now of 0.015 of total equity (~$1,494, about 4.89 of the 8.18 shares held, so roughly 3.3 shares sold at the $305.26 mark for ~$1 of 10bp friction). The bear wins the next four to eight weeks on trend structure, overhead supply and a genuinely defective entry; the bull wins the multi-year cash-generation case, which is why this is a partial trim to a residual stub with ~98.5% cash, not a liquidation. Add nothing inside the 300–309 band; the residual goes to zero only on a daily close below $299.50 on >55M shares, and re-risking waits for a daily close above $316.53 that actually reclaims the $315.81 VWMA on >55M volume, not the 310.30 hair-trigger. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October Q4 FY26 print.
final.investment_thesis:
Three of the four seats land on the same executable step and the one that does not — the conservative call for 0.0 — overreaches on the evidence actually in front of us, so 0.015 is the honest size and Underweight is the honest direction. I take the direction and the sizing from the trader and the neutral analyst, absorb the conservative's process critique into the residual-stub framework, and reject the aggressive analyst's re-entry architecture while agreeing with his conclusion.

The single strongest argument in the debate belongs to the bear, and it is arithmetic rather than narrative: the bull's trade construction is internally inconsistent. A $299.50 stop against a $305.26 entry is 5.76 points, or about 0.70x the 8.22 ATR, which the neutral analyst himself calls a coin flip versus the ~12-point (1.5x ATR) minimum; the bull then cites the 200-SMA at 280.30 as the 'strategic backstop,' an 8.1% risk. You cannot quote the tight number for the pitch and the wide number for the safety net. Re-underwritten honestly, reward-to-risk to the first target (VWMA $315.81) is roughly 1:1 on a name where the last five sessions averaged ~39.7M shares against a 55.1M trend, i.e. an absence of demand rather than an exhausted seller base. That is not an accumulate zone, and the conservative is right that because nothing in this simulation executes a narrative stop, size itself is the only risk control available.

The second decisive leg is trend structure, and it is not a wick. Ten consecutive closes below a rolling-over 50-SMA (309.79 -> 309.28), price below the 10-EMA at 310.24 and 3.34% below the VWMA at 315.81, MACD at -2.186 with a -3.035 histogram and the zero-line cross already completed on August 11, RSI at 43 with room to fall. The VWMA overhead is the key number: it means the average recent buyer is underwater, which is supply, not a springboard — and it also invalidates the aggressive and neutral 310.30 re-risk trigger, which cannot simultaneously be a breakout and sit three to six points beneath the shelf it is supposed to clear. The 06-25 flush precedent the bull leans on is disowned by the source material: that flush happened above the 50-SMA; this one is below. And the four-touch 300/302.05 shelf (300.00 on 07-31, 302.56 on 08-03, 300.57 on 08-12, 302.05 on 08-13) is being worked, not defended — each test consumes the buyers defending it, and the bull's own invalidation sits directly beneath it.

The conservative's strongest point is the one I will not dismiss: the best fundamental print in the data set — 49.07% nine-month gross margin, 50.06% in the June quarter, EPS +22.4%, nine-month FCF of $110.2B, ~$62.2B net cash, zero new long-term debt, a -55 day cash conversion cycle — was filed July 31 and the tape gapped from 333.43 into a 304.81 open and never reclaimed it. When the best news produces the worst reaction in the sample, a multiple is being repriced, and the Jefferies target cut on 'not enough product and AI momentum' is the dated expression of that. I also take his three unresolved fundamental items at face value: the effective tax rate stepping from 15.39% to 17.58% (~2.7 points of EPS that consensus may not model), roughly $15B of the CFO growth coming from AR release (AR days 34.6 -> 23.5) and ~$10.8B from lower cash taxes, buybacks down 12% YoY, and a $13.1B gross intangible build with no matching acquisition cash outflow that the source material explicitly flags for 10-Q verification — the bull used that item to confirm his Siri thesis instead of checking it, which is backwards.

Where the conservative overreaches is in jumping from 'the stop is unenforceable' to 'zero size.' That is the correct observation with the wrong conclusion in a continuous-position framework where cash earns nothing. The residual 1.5% weight loses roughly $121 on an 8.1% drawdown to the 200-SMA at 280.30 — a tolerable tail, not a reason to pay two round trips and forfeit the only thing the evidence supports, which is a live stake in a franchise still generating ~$147B annualized FCF while a range resolves. His 'repricing acute phase is behind us' rebuttal also lands: ATR has compressed from 9.87 toward 8.22 and volume has collapsed from 132.5M to ~40M, and the 200-SMA is rising (267 -> 280 in two months) with spot 8.9% above it. That is an unresolved range with a defended floor, not a broken primary trend, and it is precisely why the answer is Underweight and not Sell.

What I explicitly reject: the aggressive analyst's framing that this is a convexity trade — it is risk reduction on a ~$1,000 notional with a ~$120 tail, and his own escalation of rhetoric to 'aggressive capital' confirms the neutral's diagnosis that the framework is doing narrative work. I also reject his 0.04 re-risk at 310.30 and the neutral's 0.02 variant at the same level for the reason above: the VWMA cannot be 'reclaimed' at 315.81 by a close at 310.30. Entry above the shelf, not beneath it. And I reject the neutral's implication that Scenario D patience is free: staying long below the 50-SMA, below the 10-EMA and below the VWMA is an affirmative mean-reversion bet taken without a trigger.

Sizing against total account equity, not any standard allocation: $1,494 notional at 0.015, ~4.89 shares retained, ~3.3 sold. The $313.07 average cost is irrelevant — break-even is not a thesis, and the account has already realized -$354.95 across 0.12 -> 0.15 -> 0.065 -> 0.040 -> 0.025 in five sessions, which is the real process lesson: stop transacting the daily tape. Write the two levels down and do nothing between them.

What would change the call. Upward: a daily close above $316.53 that holds with volume above 55M and the VWMA at 315.81 genuinely reclaimed, MACD back above zero — re-enter at ~0.02 first, not 0.04. Also a signed Siri licensing deal with disclosed terms and counterparties, a gross margin print at or above 49% with AI-competitive headlines in the base, or a 10-Q footnote resolving the $13.1B intangibles build as anything other than a capitalized commitment; any of those raises the target independent of price. Downward: a daily close below $299.50 on >55M volume opens 293.50 (lower Bollinger) and then 280.30, and takes the residual to zero. Explicit gaps in the record, not papered over: no valuation multiples, no options chain or implied move, no Q4 FY26 guidance figures or forward consensus, and no coverage of the 08-06 through 08-11 news window — so the $295 target is technical, not valuation-derived, and neither the 'overreaction' nor the 'memory-cost repricing' story is established fact.
